title: The Barrow Wight
text: A wight sits cross-legged on a burial mound, thin as winter, its eyes two cold sparks. Around it on the grass lie shadows without bodies, pinned down like pelts to dry. It asks riddles, it says, and if you answer wrong it keeps your shadow.

options.label: The wisest answers its riddles, wagering their shadow on their wits.

outcomes.text: Right, every one. It hisses, and gives up a grave-good from the mound, and will not look at them.
Wrong. It reaches out and peels their shadow off the grass like a skin, and pins it down beside the others.

options.label: The shrewdest answers with a riddle of their own, and lets it puzzle.

outcomes.text: It is still thinking when you leave, cold eyes narrowed, muttering into the grass.

options.label: Say nothing at all. A thing that keeps shadows will not play fair.

outcomes.text: It unfolds from the mound, long and thin, and the shadows on the grass begin to move with it.
